ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a tilted large rectangle, and inside there is a horizontally placed gray rectangle. The gray rectangle is divided into three identical squares side by side, so the length of the gray rectangle is 3 times the side length of each small square, and the width is the side length of each small square. Two opposite corner points of the gray rectangle are located at the midpoints of the shorter sides of the large rectangle, and the other two corner points respectively touch the two longer sides of the large rectangle. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small square be s. The area of each small square is 25 cm^2, so s^2 = 25, s = 5. According to the coordinate method, set one midpoint corner of the gray rectangle as A = (0,0), and set the opposite midpoint corner as C = (3s,s). Then AC is the direction of the long side of the large rectangle, and its length is |AC| = sqrt((3s)^2 + s^2) = s√10. The other two corners of the gray rectangle are B = (3s,0) and D = (0,s), and they are respectively on the two long sides of the large rectangle. The distance from point B to line AC is |cross(AC,AB)| / |AC|. Among them AC = (3s,s), AB = (3s,0), and the magnitude of the cross product is |3s·0 - s·3s| = 3s^2, so the distance is 3s^2/(s√10) = 3s/√10. Point D is on the other side of AC, and the distance is the same, so the short side length of the large rectangle is 2·3s/√10 = 6s/√10. Therefore the area of the large rectangle is (s√10)(6s/√10) = 6s^2 = 6·25 = 150.
